sections.h2: Where is Lincoln County, Missouri, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Lincoln County sits in eastern Missouri, with the Mississippi River forming its border with Illinois and Troy as the county seat. It belongs to the St. Louis metropolitan area. Wikipedia lists 640 square miles of total area, 627 of them land, and Pike, Calhoun (Illinois), St. Charles, Warren and Montgomery counties adjoin it.

The county was founded on December 14, 1818 and is named for Major General Benjamin Lincoln of the Revolutionary War. It has grown fast: the Census Bureau counted 52,566 residents in 2010, 59,574 in 2020 and estimated 66,676 for July 2025, a rise of 11.9% over the 2020 base.

That growth shows up in the permits. The Census Bureau reports 252 building permits for 2025, and 24,289 housing units as of July 2025.

sections.h2: Which school districts and communities serve Lincoln County?
sections.html:
Five Missouri districts are based in or serve the county, and your tax bill carries the levy of the one that covers your address. The Lincoln County R-III district in Troy is the largest, with Troy Buchanan High School and New Horizons High School.

  • Lincoln County R-III (Troy), with elementary schools such as Boone, Cuivre Park, Hawk Point and Main Street
  • Elsberry R-II
  • Silex R-I
  • Winfield R-IV
  • Wright City R-II, which serves southern parts of the county

The Wikipedia entry also lists Moscow Mills, Old Monroe, Winfield, Foley, Truxton and Whiteside among the communities. Moscow Mills and Old Monroe sit in the southeast corner, closest to St. Charles County.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Lincoln County homes and incomes?
sections.html:
The median owner-occupied home in Lincoln County is worth $244,300, based on 2020 to 2024 Census data, and 79.0% of households own. Median household income is $89,278 in 2024 dollars, and 7.9% of residents live in poverty.

sections.h2: Who assesses and who collects property tax in Lincoln County?
sections.html:
Kevin Bishop is the County Assessor, at 3 Front Street in Troy, and Jessica Zumwalt is the Collector of Revenue, at 1 Front Street in Troy. The Collector's taxpayer portal gives 636-528-0316 as the office phone and lets you search records by name, statement number or parcel number.

The Assessor's page describes three parts of every tax bill: the assessment authority sets value, the taxing authority (school, city, fire district and others) sets the rate from its budget, and the collection authority collects the amount. The Assessor has no say over tax rates.

The Collector's office handles current and delinquent tax for the state, county, ambulance, hospital, SB-40 board, county health center, schools, cities and fire districts. It also collects drainage and neighborhood improvement district charges and merchant license fees, and processes escrow payments for mortgage holders.

sections.h2: How does Lincoln County assess residential property?
sections.html:
Residential property is assessed at 19% of market value, farmland at 12%, and commercial property at 32%. The Assessor reappraises every odd-numbered year (2021, 2023, 2025), with values set as of January 1, and uses even-numbered years to pick up new construction and lost improvements.

Field appraisers visit parcels each year. They drive marked county vehicles and carry ID badges, and the office asks you to call if someone without identification is on your land. In reassessment years, the office compares recent sale prices with its appraisals to decide whether land and structures move up.

If you see a value change, the Assessor must send a Notice of Change in Value. You may ask for an informal hearing, then appear before the Board of Equalization. The filing deadline is the second Monday in July, and the Board convenes the third Monday in July. After that comes the State Tax Commission.

sections.h2: What dates matter for Lincoln County property tax?
sections.html:
The tax year starts with a January 1 valuation and ends with a December 31 payment date. Real estate transfers are posted to the new owner through August 31 of the tax year, so a statement for a house sold after that date still goes out in the old owner's name.

  • January 1: assessment date for real property
  • Second Monday in July: appeal deadline for the Board of Equalization
  • Third Monday in July: Board of Equalization convenes
  • Second week of July: tax sale list begins running in the Lincoln County Journal and Elsberry Democrat
  • Fourth Monday in August, 10 a.m.: tax sale on the courthouse east steps
  • December 31: tax due, and the State Tax Commission notes penalties and interest after that date

If you receive a statement for a house you sold after August 31, the Assessor's page says to contact the County Collector about forwarding it to the new owner. Check the closing statement from the title company to see how each party's share of the taxes was credited.

sections.h2: How does the Lincoln County tax sale work?
sections.html:
Real estate with three years of delinquent tax must be offered at the annual tax sale, held on the fourth Monday in August at 10 a.m. on the east steps of the courthouse. The owner can pay in full before the sale, and the collector says a high share of owners do so after the advertisement runs.

Bidders register from 8 a.m. in the Collector's office, Room 103, sign an affidavit that they owe no delinquent tax, and must be present to bid. A bidder from outside Missouri has to name a Lincoln County citizen as agent. Opening bids cover the taxes, interest and charges.

The purchaser gets a certificate of purchase, pays later taxes, and has no right to possession during the one-year redemption period. Money bid above the opening amount goes to the county treasurer for the owner of record, and unclaimed surplus goes to the schools after three years. The Collector's office advises buyers to see an attorney first.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Lincoln County tax bill?
sections.html:
Use the Collector's taxpayer portal, call the office, or visit 1 Front Street in Troy. Search by statement number (for example R plus the number for real estate), by parcel number or by owner name, and the portal returns up to 100 records.

The state's rule is that a mailed payment must carry a postmark no later than December 31, and that the full bill must be paid to the collector by then if you want to pay under protest. Write "paid under protest" on the check and attach a statement with your grounds and your opinion of fair market value.

If an LLC, trust, estate or corporation owns the parcel, an attorney must file any State Tax Commission appeal. A taxpayer who missed notice of an increase, or who bought within 30 days of the statement mailing, may appeal directly to the Commission.

sections.h2: What should I check before selling a Lincoln County house with tax due?
sections.html:
Pull your parcel record, ask the Collector for a payoff, and confirm the Assessor has the correct owner and acreage. Owners in newer subdivisions near the St. Charles County line often have special district charges on the bill, so ask which ones apply.

  • Compare your statement with the closing statement the title company prepares.
  • Ask whether any year is on the August tax sale list.
  • Ask the Collector about senior relief programs if the seller is an older homeowner.
  • Confirm that a transfer recorded after August 31 will send the next statement to you, not the buyer.

A seller who cannot repair or carry the house can sell for cash as-is, and the payoff is then settled at the table from the price.

faqs.q: When are Lincoln County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due by December 31. A mailed payment needs a postmark on or before that date to avoid penalty and interest.

faqs.q: When does the Lincoln County tax sale take place?
faqs.a: It takes place on the fourth Monday in August at 10 a.m. on the east steps of the courthouse in Troy. Registration starts at 8 a.m. in Room 103.

faqs.q: How often does Lincoln County reassess real estate?
faqs.a: Every two years, in odd-numbered years such as 2025 and 2027, with a January 1 value date. Even-numbered years cover new construction and lost improvements.

faqs.q: What is the Lincoln County Board of Equalization deadline?
faqs.a: The filing deadline is the second Monday in July, and the Board convenes on the third Monday in July.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Lincoln County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Collector of Revenue at 636-528-0316 about amounts owed. For a value question, contact the Assessor's office at 3 Front Street in Troy.
